props.description: 16, 24, 32, 40, 96 or 128px across: Atlassian's avatar sizes. Initials step up from 12px to 32px with it; `xs` shows the first letter only.

props.name: imageSrc
props.description: The picture, cropped to fill the circle. If it fails to load, the initials or the silhouette show instead.

props.name: imageAlt
props.description: Who this is. Names the whole avatar. Without it the avatar is decorative and hidden from assistive tech.

props.name: initials
props.description: One or two letters, shown when there is no image. Pass the letters, not a name: they are uppercased by style. `xs` shows the first only.

props.name: variant
props.description: `subtle` is a tint of the hue; `solid` is its fill (600 in light, 400 in dark).

props.name: statusLabel
props.description: The status word in the name, for another language.

anatomy.name: Container
anatomy.description: The circle, in the chosen colour and variant. Clips its content and carries the name.

anatomy.name: Image
anatomy.description: Cropped to fill. Silent itself: the name is on the container.

anatomy.name: Initials
anatomy.description: Shown when there is no image, or it fails to load.

anatomy.name: Silhouette
anatomy.description: A head and shoulders, when there is neither.

anatomy.name: Status dot
anatomy.description: Optional. Presence, on the bottom-end corner, in a ring of the page colour. Part of the name.

anatomy.name: Group
anatomy.description: Optional. Avatars overlapping by 4px, each ringed in the page colour.

anatomy.name: More
anatomy.description: A neutral avatar with "+n" for the people past `max`. Named only when the avatars are.

whenToUse:
Use an Avatar to show who: the author of a comment, the people on a
project, the account that is signed in. Give it `imageAlt` when the avatar
is the only thing that says who it is. When the name is printed next to
it, leave `imageAlt` out: the avatar is decorative, and the name is read
once.
whenNotToUse:
- **For a product, team or workspace logo.** An Avatar is always round, so
  it reads as a person. Use an image with its own shape.
- **For status through colour.** The avatar's `color` means nothing. Use
  `status` for presence, and print the status where people act on it (an
  assignee picker): a dot is a glance, not the only cue.
- **For a long list of people.** A group shows who at a glance; past a
  handful, show the count or a list of names instead.
- **For an icon in a circle.** Use the icon itself, or an icon-only
  [Button](?path=/docs/components-buttons-button--docs) when it acts.

do.caption: The name is printed, so the avatar has no imageAlt. A screen reader hears “Mary Thompson” once.

dont.caption: imageAlt repeats the printed name: “Mary Thompson, image, Mary Thompson”.

sections.title: Accessibility
blocks: - `imageAlt` names the **whole avatar** (`role="img"`), not just the image, so the image, the initials and the silhouette all announce the same person. The inner `` has `alt=""`. - Without `imageAlt` the avatar is **decorative** and hidden (`aria-hidden`), its status dot with it. - With `status`, the status **joins the name**: "Mary Thompson, Online". The dot itself is not read. - In a group, the "+n" is named "3 more" when the avatars are named, and decorative when they are not. - With `hasTooltips`, the "+n" is the one avatar that takes focus, with the focus ring, and its tooltip of hidden names is its description. The other avatars' tooltips open on hover only: their names are already their accessible names. - Initials are never read out: with `imageAlt` the avatar's name replaces them, without it the avatar is hidden. They are uppercased with CSS, so the text keeps the letters as passed. - Initials meet 4.5:1 in every colour and variant, on every gray ramp in both modes, measured by the `Contrast` story. Neutral solid is gray 600 under gray 50, 6.5:1 or more. - On `subtle` the silhouette uses the initials colour (neutral uses `--color-text-subtlest`), past the 3:1 a graphic needs. - On `solid` the silhouette is **always white**, by choice. In light mode that is under 3:1 on the warm hues (orange to lime); in dark mode, where the fill is the lighter 400 step, on most hues. It is accepted because the silhouette carries no information: the name is in `imageAlt` or printed beside the avatar.

props.name: count
props.description: The number shown. Nothing renders without `count` or `isDot`. `0` shows "0".

props.name: variant
props.description: Colour. `accent` is the inverted neutral. For presence: `success` Online, `warning` Away, `destructive` Busy, `secondary` Offline.

props.name: size
props.description: Size of a dot: 8px (`md`) or 6px (`sm`). A count is 16px tall at either size; `sm` on a count is deprecated and renders the `md` badge.

props.name: isDot
props.description: A dot with no number: "something new", not "how many". Hidden from assistive tech unless it has `aria-label`.

props.name: maxCount
props.description: Counts above this show as `maxCount+`, e.g. `99+`, so a large number does not stretch the badge.

props.name: isFloating
props.description: Pins the badge to a corner of `children`, with a ring in the page colour. Hidden from assistive tech.

props.name: floatingPlacement
props.description: The corner a floating badge sits on. Start and end are physical: left and right.

anatomy.name: Anchor
anatomy.description: Wraps the element a floating badge pins to.

anatomy.name: Container
anatomy.description: The box and its count, in tabular figures. Past maxCount, a "+" follows. Floating, it gets a ring in the page colour.

anatomy.name: Dot
anatomy.description: The container with no count: something new, not how many.

whenToUse:
Use a Badge to say something is new, or how many, on the element it
belongs to: unread messages on an inbox button, a status dot on an avatar.
A floating badge is hidden from assistive tech, so the element it sits on
carries the meaning in its own name.

Colour is never the only signal. A destructive badge still needs words
somewhere that say what is wrong, and a status dot needs `aria-label` or
a name beside it.
whenNotToUse:
- **For a label or category.** Use a
  [Tag](?path=/docs/components-atomic-elements-tag--docs): it holds words,
  a badge holds a number.
- **For a message that needs reading.** Use an Alert or a Toast.
- **On every item of a list.** A badge flags what is new; if everything
  is, nothing stands out.

do.caption: The button is named “Notifications, 4 unread”: the count reaches a screen reader too.

dont.caption: The count lives only in the badge, which is hidden: a screen reader hears “Notifications”.

sections.title: Accessibility
blocks:
- An **inline count** is plain text and is read where it sits. Inside a
  button it becomes part of the name ("Inbox 12").
- A **floating** badge is hidden from assistive tech: it sits *outside*
  the element it decorates, so it would be read as a stray number after
  it. Put the meaning in that element's name instead:
  `aria-label="Notifications, 4 unread"`.
- A **dot** has no text and is hidden too.
- Pass `aria-label` to any badge to expose it as an image with that name
  instead, e.g. a status dot on an avatar: `aria-label="Online"`.
- Contrast is checked by addon-a11y in error mode for every story.

props.name: orientation
props.description: Horizontal between stacked blocks; vertical between items in a row, where it stretches to the row.

props.name: inset
props.description: Indents both ends so the line stops short of its container: 16px horizontal, 8px vertical.

props.name: size
props.description: Line thickness: 1px, 2px or 4px.

props.name: appearance
props.description: Line style. The spec's `variant`: here `variant` always means colour.

anatomy.name: Line
anatomy.description: An <hr>, drawn as a border in the border colour.

whenToUse:
Use a Divider between groups that spacing alone does not separate: the
sections of a menu, the blocks of a settings page, groups in a toolbar.
Divide groups, not every item: a line after each row turns a list into
stripes and makes the real breaks harder to see.
whenNotToUse:
- **Where space already separates.** Cards, list items with padding and
  headed sections are grouped by their own whitespace; a line adds noise.
- **As the only thing that tells groups apart.** The line is faint on
  purpose (see Accessibility). Pair it with a heading or space.
- **For a border of a component.** Draw that with the component's own
  border, not a Divider beside it.

do.caption: One line between two groups: the break carries meaning.

dont.caption: A line after every item: nothing stands out as a group.

sections.title: Accessibility
blocks:
- `<hr>` is announced as a separator. Vertical dividers add
  `aria-orientation="vertical"`; horizontal ones don't, because that is
  already the default.
- If the line is purely decorative, e.g. between two icons that are
  already grouped, pass `aria-hidden` so it isn't announced at all.
- The `--color-border` colour is below 3:1 against the background on purpose: a
  divider is decoration and is not required to meet the non-text contrast
  ratio. Never let a divider be the only thing that tells groups apart.

props.name: children
props.description: One key: a glyph (`⌘`, `⇧`, `↵`) or a short word (`Esc`, `Tab`). Ignored when `keys` is set.

props.name: size
props.description: 20px (`md`) or 16px (`sm`) tall. `sm` fits inside a small control or a dense row.

anatomy.name: Key
anatomy.description: One key cap: a glyph or a short word on a bordered chip, its lower edge thicker like a raised key.

anatomy.name: Group
anatomy.description: Optional, with `keys`: the outer `<kbd>` that holds a combination, the caps a small gap apart.

whenToUse:
Use Kbd wherever the page tells someone which key to press: a hint in a
tooltip, a command palette row, a line of help text, a shortcuts sheet.
These are places where people come to learn a shortcut, so the key gets a
cap. A Menu is not: see below.

Match the platform: ⌘ and ⌥ on a Mac, Ctrl and Alt elsewhere. Kbd shows
what it is given and does not detect the platform.
whenNotToUse:
- **For a Menu item's shortcut.** Use Menu's `shortcut` string: menus
  show shortcuts as quiet text at the end of the row, the way desktop
  menus do. The menu is for acting, and a cap on every row would pull the
  eye from the labels. A command palette is the exception: it is where
  shortcuts are discovered, so its rows use Kbd.
- **For code or a value someone types.** Use `<code>`: Kbd is a key, not
  text to copy.
- **To bind the key.** Kbd is display only; the page binds the shortcut.

do.caption: Inside a control the caps are hidden and the button says Meta+K through aria-keyshortcuts: its name stays “Search”.

dont.caption: Left in, the glyphs join the name: a screen reader hears “Search ⌘ K”, and ⌘ is read as “place of interest”.

sections.title: Accessibility
blocks:
- Kbd is a native `<kbd>`; a combination is a `<kbd>` of `<kbd>`s, one
  per key.
- It is not focusable and has no role: it is never in the tab order.
- In running text it is read where it sits, as text: "Press Esc to close".
  A combination's keys are read one after the other with no "plus" (⌘S);
  write the combination out in the sentence when that matters.
- Inside a control, hide it with `aria-hidden` and put the shortcut on the
  control with `aria-keyshortcuts` (for example `Meta+K`), so the
  control's name stays its label.
- Contrast is checked by addon-a11y in error mode for every story.

props.name: size
props.description: Deprecated. Every tag is 20px tall; `sm` renders the same tag as `md` and will be removed in the next release.

props.name: appearance
props.description: `subtle` tint, `outlined` border, or `solid` fill. Solid hue tags fall under 4.5:1 on warm hues.

props.description: Adds a remove button named "Remove `text`".

anatomy.description: The box: fill, border and corner by appearance and variant.

anatomy.name: Start icon
anatomy.description: Optional and decorative. A start avatar takes its place when given.

anatomy.name: Text
anatomy.description: Truncates with an ellipsis rather than wrapping.

whenToUse:
Use a Tag to label or categorise: a status on a row, the categories of an
item, the filters applied to a list, the people picked in a field. Where a
tag has to pass AA, use `subtle` or `outlined`: solid hue tags keep one
white label across hues, which the warm ones carry under 4.5:1.

Colour carries meaning here, so it is never the only signal: the text says
what the status is.

In a wrapped list of removable tags on touch, keep at least `--space-6`
between rows. The remove button's touch area reaches 12px above and below
a 20px tag, and neighbouring targets would overlap.
whenNotToUse:
- **For an action.** A tag is a label; its only control is remove. Use a
  [Button](?path=/docs/components-buttons-button--docs).
- **For a choice the user toggles on and off.** Use a
  [Toggle Button](?path=/docs/components-buttons-togglebutton--docs) or a
  Checkbox.
- **For a count.** Use a
  [Badge](?path=/docs/components-atomic-elements-badge--docs).

do.caption: Warm hues in subtle: every label clears 4.5:1.

dont.caption: The same hues solid: the white label falls under 4.5:1.

sections.title: Accessibility
blocks:
- The remove button is named **"Remove `text`"** (e.g. "Remove Design"),
  so a list of tags does not read as a row of identical "Remove" buttons.
- It is a native `<button>`: Tab to reach, Enter or Space to press.
- On touch screens (`pointer: coarse`) its hit area grows to 44×44px
  without changing how the tag looks. That area reaches 12px above and
  below a 20px tag.
- After a tag is removed, focus has nowhere to stay and drops to the page.
  If that matters, move it to the next tag's remove button, or to the
  field the tags belong to, in your `onRemove`.
- The icon and the avatar are decorative.
- Every label clears 4.5:1 in both themes, measured by the `Contrast`
  story, except solid hue tags (see Differences from the spec).

props.name: variant

props.name: appearance
props.description: Emphasis: `contained` for the main action, `outlined` and `ghost` for the rest.

props.description: Fills the width of its container.

props.description: Square, for an icon with no visible label. Requires `aria-label`: a type error without it.

props.description: Native `disabled`: dimmed and out of the tab order. On a link, drops `href`.

whenToUse:
Use a Button for an action on the current page: save, submit, open a
dialog, delete. Use one `primary contained` button per view, for the thing
to do next. Everything else steps down to `outlined` or `ghost`, or to
`secondary`.

**Loading** keeps the button's width and focus and blocks it from acting
again, so a double-submit is impossible and a keyboard user is not dropped
back to the top of the page.
whenNotToUse:
- **To navigate.** A link is not a button. Pass `href` and Button renders a
  real `<a>`: it keeps link semantics, opens in a new tab on middle-click,
  and gets the link cursor. A plain Button with an `onClick` that changes
  the page does none of that.
- **For a setting that stays on or off.** Use a
  [Toggle Button](?path=/docs/components-buttons-togglebutton--docs), a
  Switch or a Checkbox.
- **For a link inside running text.** Use Link.

do.caption: One primary button: the thing to do next. The rest step down.

dont.caption: Two primary buttons compete for the same click.

do.caption: Show progress with isLoading: the button stays where focus is, and cannot fire twice.

dont.caption: Disabling it to show progress drops keyboard focus and reads as unavailable.

sections.title: Accessibility
blocks:
- A native `<button>`, `type="button"` by default so it never submits a
  form by accident. Enter and Space both activate it.
- `isIconOnly` needs `aria-label`; TypeScript refuses it without one.
  Icons are `aria-hidden` everywhere else, so they never double the name.
- `isLoading` sets `aria-busy` and `aria-disabled` but keeps the button
  focusable. `disabled` removes it from the tab order, as native buttons
  do.
- A disabled or loading link renders a bare `<a>` with no `href` (the
  only thing that stops an `<a>` navigating) and `aria-disabled`. With
  `render`, the render element is dropped too, since a router's Link would
  keep its own `href`.
- `render` is for elements that are already interactive: a link or a
  router's Link. It merges props onto the element and adds no role or
  keyboard handling, so do not render a `<div>` through it.
- Hover and pressed keep the label at 4.5:1 too. The `StateContrast`
  story measures every variant × appearance × state under all seventeen
  accents in both modes, from the CSS that ships.
- `sm` and `md` are under 44px; on touch screens (`pointer: coarse`) the
  hit area grows to 44×44px without the button growing.
- Focus ring: 2px `--color-border-focused`, 2px offset, at 3:1 or better on the page.

props.name: multiple
props.description: Any number pressed at once. Without it, one at a time (a segmented control): once one is pressed, pressing it again keeps it pressed.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables every toggle in the group.

anatomy.name: Container
anatomy.description: ToggleGroup joins its toggles: inner corners square, borders shared. ButtonGroup spaces its buttons 4px apart.

anatomy.name: Button
anatomy.description: A ToggleButton (or a Button in ButtonGroup), with a label or an icon.

anatomy.name: Selected
anatomy.description: The pressed toggle: one at a time, or several with `multiple`.

whenToUse:
Use `ToggleGroup` when the toggles answer one question (which view, which
filters) and `ButtonGroup` when a few actions belong together. Give every
button in a group the same variant and appearance, so the pressed one is
the only one that stands out.
whenNotToUse:
- **To switch between panels of content.** Use Tabs: they own the panel
  and its `tabpanel` role.
- **For a choice submitted with a form.** Use a Radio group or Checkboxes:
  a toggle applies at once, a form field waits for Submit.
- **For unrelated actions.** Lay out separate Buttons with a wider gap;
  a group says they belong together.
- **For more than a handful of options.** Use a Select.

do.caption: One look across the group: only the pressed segment stands out.

dont.caption: A different variant per button reads as several states at once.

sections.title: Accessibility
blocks:
- Both containers have `role="group"`; name them with `aria-label`.
- Each toggle is a native `<button>` with `aria-pressed`, so a screen reader
  announces "Board, toggle button, pressed".
- A `ToggleGroup` is one tab stop. Arrow keys move between its toggles
  and wrap, Home and End jump to the first and last; Space or Enter
  presses.
- Single choice keeps one pressed: pressing the pressed toggle again does
  not release it.
- A `ButtonGroup`'s buttons are each a tab stop, with no `aria-pressed`.
- A disabled `ToggleGroup` disables every toggle in it.
- An icon-only button needs its own `aria-label`, as on Button. A
  [Tooltip](?path=/docs/components-overlays-tooltip--docs) can show that
  label to sighted users: it merges onto the button instead of wrapping
  it, so the group still holds only its buttons.

whenToUse:
Use a toggle for a setting that is on or off and applies immediately:
Bold, Follow, a filter. The label names the setting, and stays the same in
both states.
whenNotToUse:
- **For a choice submitted with a form.** Use a Checkbox or a Switch: a
  toggle applies at once, a form field waits for Submit.
- **For one of many.** Put the toggles in a
  [ToggleGroup](?path=/docs/components-buttons-buttongroup--docs), or use
  radios or Tabs. A lone toggle is independent: pressing one does not
  release another.
- **For an action.** Something that happens once (Save, Send) is a
  [Button](?path=/docs/components-buttons-button--docs).

do.caption: The label names the setting; pressed says it is on. A screen reader hears “Follow, toggle button, pressed”.

dont.caption: A label that flips to the action reads as “Unfollow, pressed”, which contradicts itself.

sections.title: Accessibility
blocks:
- A native `<button>` with `aria-pressed`, so a screen reader announces
  "Subscribe, toggle button, pressed".
- **Keep the label the same in both states.** `aria-pressed` carries the
  state; a label that switches from "Follow" to "Unfollow" as well reads
  as "Unfollow, pressed", which contradicts itself.
- Enter and Space both toggle it.
- `isIconOnly` needs `aria-label`, as on Button.
- `isLoading` keeps it focusable but inert, as on Button.
- 44×44px touch target at `sm` and `md`, from Button.

whenToUse:
Use a checkbox for a choice that is submitted with a form: accepting
terms, opting in, picking several items from a list. Nothing happens
until the form is sent.
Write the label so that checked means yes.
whenNotToUse:
- **For a setting that applies at once.** Use a
  [Switch](?path=/docs/components-controls-switch--docs): it acts like a
  light switch, a checkbox waits for Submit.
- **For one choice out of several.** Use a
  [Radio](?path=/docs/components-controls-radio--docs) group; checkboxes
  are independent.
- **For a toggle in a toolbar.** Use a
  [Toggle Button](?path=/docs/components-buttons-togglebutton--docs).

do.caption: The label says what checking does: checked means yes.

dont.caption: A negative label makes unchecked a double negative, and readers stop to work it out.

sections.title: Accessibility
blocks:
- `role="checkbox"` with `aria-checked`, `mixed` when indeterminate.
  Space toggles it.
- The label wraps the box, so it names it and clicking it toggles the box.
- `helperText` is the box's description; the error state sets
  `aria-invalid`.
- The unchecked outline is `--color-border-bold`, 3:1 on the page on every
  gray ramp.
- A hidden native input carries `name`, `value` and `required` into form
  submission and validation.
- The hit area is 24×24px, 44×44px on coarse pointers, without the box
  growing.

anatomy.description: A slider round the colour wheel, 0 to 359 degrees.

anatomy.name: Opacity strip
anatomy.description: 0 to 100%, over a checkerboard. Hidden with `alpha={false}`.

anatomy.name: Format menu
anatomy.description: The kit’s Select: Hex, RGB, HSL or HSB, which the channel fields follow.

anatomy.name: Channel fields
anatomy.description: One field box: the hex, or three numbers, then opacity in %.

anatomy.name: Swatches
anatomy.description: Optional presets under a divider. The chosen one has a ring.

whenToUse:
Use a colour picker when any colour is a valid answer: a brand colour, a
chart series, a label someone defines. When there is a palette to follow,
offer it as named swatches.
whenNotToUse:
- **For a few fixed colours.** When only a set of colours is allowed (tag
  colours, a theme accent), use a
  [Radio](?path=/docs/components-controls-radio--docs) group of swatches or
  a Select: the picker lets anyone type any colour.
- **To show a colour.** Use a swatch and its hex as text.

do.caption: The colours people should use, as named swatches: one click, and a screen reader says “Blue”, not a hex.

dont.caption: A palette to follow but no swatches: people match it by eye and land a few steps off.

sections.title: Accessibility
blocks:
- The field is a text input named by its label. The swatch button is
  named "Choose colour, #3b82f6 selected", and the popover is a dialog
  named "Choose colour" that returns focus to the button on Escape.
- The area is one tab stop: a slider named "Saturation" whose value text
  reads both numbers ("Saturation 76%, brightness 96%"). Left and right
  change saturation, up and down brightness, Shift moves 10%, Page Up and
  Page Down change brightness by 10%, Home and End set saturation to 0 or
  100%. A second "Brightness" slider is there for a screen reader's
  browse mode.
- The hue strip is a slider named "Hue", read as "217 degrees"; the
  opacity strip, "Opacity", read as "50%".
- The format menu is the kit's Select, named "Colour format". Channel
  fields are text inputs named for what they hold ("Red", "Hue degrees",
  "Lightness percent", "Opacity percent", "Hex"), so they do not share a
  name with the sliders.
- Swatches are native radios in a radio group named "Swatches": one tab
  stop, arrows move and choose, and the chosen one is checked. None is
  checked while the colour is not one of them. They are 24px with 8px
  between them, which meets WCAG 2.5.8 without a larger invisible target.
- A colour is never the only way to know the value: the hex is always in
  the field.

props.name: label
props.description: The group's legend: names the radiogroup.

props.name: helperText
props.description: Under the whole group. The error message when `validationState` is `error`, and then on every radio.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: Starting selection when uncontrolled. None selected when left out.

props.name: variant
props.description: Colour of the selected radio: `neutral` (the foreground) or `primary` (the accent).

props.name: orientation
props.description: Stacked or in a row that wraps. Layout only: arrow keys work either way.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Every radio dimmed, and the selection cannot change.

props.name: required
props.description: One must be selected to submit. Adds an asterisk to the legend.

props.name: readOnly
props.description: Focusable and submitted, but the selection cannot change.

props.name: validationState
props.description: `error` sets `aria-invalid` on every radio, turns the outlines and the group message red; `success` turns the message green.

anatomy.name: Legend
anatomy.description: Names the group. Optional, but a group without one needs `aria-label`.

anatomy.name: Radio
anatomy.description: The 16px circle: an outline when unselected.

anatomy.name: Dot
anatomy.description: Shown in the selected radio, which fills with the variant.

anatomy.name: Option label
anatomy.description: Names its radio. Part of the click target.

anatomy.name: Option helper
anatomy.description: Optional. Describes one option, indented under its label.

anatomy.name: Group helper
anatomy.description: Optional. Under the whole group; the error message in the error state.

whenToUse:
Use radios to choose one option from a short list, when seeing every
option at once helps the choice: a plan, a delivery method, a size. Up to
about six options. Select the usual choice by default when there is one.
whenNotToUse:
- **For more than about six options, or options that do not fit on
  screen.** Use a Select, or a Combobox when the reader knows what to type.
- **For several choices at once.** Use
  [Checkboxes](?path=/docs/components-controls-checkbox--docs).
- **For a single on or off.** Use a
  [Checkbox](?path=/docs/components-controls-checkbox--docs) in a form, or a
  [Switch](?path=/docs/components-controls-switch--docs) for a setting
  that applies at once.

do.caption: A few options, all in view, the usual one already selected.

dont.caption: Ten radios are a wall to scan. A long list belongs in a Select or a Combobox.

sections.title: Accessibility
blocks:
- A `<fieldset>` with a `<legend>`, exposed as a `radiogroup` named by
  the legend.
- **One tab stop for the group.** Tab enters at the selected radio (or
  the first), arrow keys move and select, Tab leaves. Disabled options
  are skipped.
- Each option's helper text is its own description. Plain group help
  describes the group once; an error message reaches every radio, so
  whichever has focus says what is wrong.
- The unselected outline is `--color-border-bold`, 3:1 on the page.
- A hidden native input carries `name` and `required` into form
  submission and validation.
- Each radio's hit area is 24×24px, 44×44px on coarse pointers.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: Starting score when uncontrolled.

props.name: max
props.description: How many stars.

props.name: size
props.description: Stars of 16px (`sm`), 24px (`md`) or 32px (`lg`).

props.name: readOnly
props.description: Shows a rating rather than asking for one: one image, read once, fractions drawn part-filled.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Dimmed, and cannot be changed.

props.name: label
props.description: Visible label over the stars; names the group.

anatomy.name: Label
anatomy.description: Optional. Names the group; without it, pass `aria-label`.

anatomy.name: Filled star
anatomy.description: Up to the score, in the bright amber.

anatomy.name: Empty star
anatomy.description: After the score, outlined. Each star holds an invisible radio.

whenToUse:
Use a rating to ask for, or show, a quick score on a short scale: a
review, a difficulty, how useful something was. Keep the scale short:
five stars is the convention readers already know.
whenNotToUse:
- **For a precise number.** Use a
  [Slider](?path=/docs/components-controls-slider--docs) or a Number Input.
- **For a choice between named options.** Use a
  [Radio](?path=/docs/components-controls-radio--docs) group, so the
  options say what they mean.
- **To show progress.** Use a Progress Bar.

do.caption: Five stars: few enough to hit and to tell apart at a glance.

dont.caption: Ten stars are small targets, and 7 looks much like 8. Use a Slider or a Number Input for a fine scale.

sections.title: Accessibility
blocks:
- Interactive: a `<fieldset>` named by its legend (or `aria-label`), with
  one radio per star named "1 out of 5 stars" and so on (change the words
  with `getValueText`). Arrows move the choice; Tab moves into and out of
  the group.
- Read-only: `role="img"` named with the value, "4.5 out of 5 stars".
- Hover previews the score; focus shows the 2px ring round the star.
- A filled star differs from an empty one by shape as well as colour.
- Stars grow a 44px target on coarse pointers.

props.name: min
props.description: The lowest value.

props.name: max
props.description: The highest value.

props.name: step
props.description: What an arrow key moves by, and the values a drag snaps to.

props.name: largeStep
props.description: What Page Up, Page Down and Shift with an arrow move by.

props.name: label
props.description: Visible label over the track; also the name of a single thumb.

props.name: showValue
props.description: Shows the value, or the range, after the label.

props.name: size
props.description: A 20px thumb on a 6px track (`md`), or 16px on 4px with a 12px label (`sm`).

props.name: orientation
props.description: A vertical slider is 12rem tall; arrow keys follow the axis.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Dims the control and stops it moving. The label and value stay readable.

anatomy.name: Label
anatomy.description: Optional. Names a single thumb.

anatomy.name: Value
anatomy.description: Optional, with `showValue`: the value or range, formatted, in tabular figures.

anatomy.name: Track
anatomy.description: The full range.

anatomy.name: Indicator
anatomy.description: The filled part: from the start to the thumb, or between two thumbs.

anatomy.name: Thumb
anatomy.description: One per value. Drag it, or focus it and use the keys.

whenToUse:
Use a slider when an approximate value is fine and seeing it change helps:
volume, brightness, a price range to filter by. Show the value with
`showValue` so the reader knows where they landed.
whenNotToUse:
- **For an exact number** (a price, a quantity). Use a Number Input, or
  pair one with the slider.
- **For a few named options.** Use a
  [Radio](?path=/docs/components-controls-radio--docs) group, so each
  option says what it means.
- **For a score out of five.** Use a
  [Rating](?path=/docs/components-controls-rating--docs).

do.caption: An approximate value, with the number shown as it moves.

dont.caption: An exact figure on a long scale: 137 out of 500 is fiddly to hit by dragging. Use a Number Input.

sections.title: Accessibility
blocks:
- Each thumb is a `role="slider"` (a real range input) with
  `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax` and a formatted
  `aria-valuetext`.
- A single thumb is named by `label`, or `aria-label`; a range needs
  `thumbLabels` so each thumb says which end it is.
- Keyboard: arrows move by `step`, Page Up / Page Down and Shift+arrows
  by `largeStep`, Home and End jump to `min` and `max`.
- The fill clears 3:1 on the track for every accent.
- Thumbs keep their size and grow a 44px hit area on coarse pointers.

props.name: defaultChecked
props.description: Starting state when uncontrolled.

props.name: label
props.description: Names the setting. Clicking it toggles the switch.

props.name: helperText
props.description: Under the label: the description, or the error message when `validationState` is `error`.

props.name: value
props.description: Submitted under `name` when on, like a checkbox.

props.name: size
props.description: Track 32×16 (`md`) or 40×20px (`lg`). `sm` is deprecated: it draws the `md` track and will be removed in the next release.

props.name: variant
props.description: Colour of the on state. `accent` is the inverted neutral; `destructive` for a setting that is risky to turn on.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Dimmed, and cannot be changed.

props.name: required
props.description: Must be on to submit. Adds an asterisk to the label.

props.name: readOnly
props.description: Focusable and submitted, but cannot be changed.

props.name: validationState
props.description: `error` sets `aria-invalid`, draws a red edge inside the track and turns the helper red; `success` turns the helper green.

anatomy.name: Track
anatomy.description: The pill: `--color-border-bold` when off, the variant’s solid when on.

anatomy.name: Thumb
anatomy.description: Slides to the end when on.

anatomy.name: Label
anatomy.description: Names the setting. Part of the click target.

anatomy.name: Helper text
anatomy.description: Optional. Indented under the label; the error message in the error state.

whenToUse:
Use a switch for a setting that takes effect the moment it is flipped,
like a light switch: dark mode, notifications, auto-save.
whenNotToUse:
- **For a choice submitted with a form.** Use a
  [Checkbox](?path=/docs/components-controls-checkbox--docs).
- **For more than two options.** Use a
  [Radio](?path=/docs/components-controls-radio--docs) group or a Select.
- **For a toggle in a toolbar** (Bold, a filter). Use a
  [Toggle Button](?path=/docs/components-buttons-togglebutton--docs).

do.caption: The setting applies as soon as the switch moves.

dont.caption: A switch that waits for Save looks done when it is not. Use a checkbox in a form.

sections.title: Accessibility
blocks:
- `role="switch"` with `aria-checked`; Space toggles it.
- The label wraps the control, so it names it and clicking it toggles it.
- `helperText` is the switch's description (`aria-describedby`); in the
  error state the switch has `aria-invalid`.
- The off track is `--color-border-bold`, measured at 3:1 on the page on
  every gray ramp; the thumb is 4.5:1 or more against its track in both
  states.
- A hidden `<input type="checkbox">` carries `name`, `value` and
  `required` into native form submission and validation.
- On is the end side: in a right-to-left page the thumb travels left.
- The hit area is at least 24px tall, 44×44px on coarse pointers.

props.name: locale
props.description: BCP 47 tag, e.g. `vi-VN`, for the month and weekday names and the first day of the week.

props.name: weekStartsOn
props.description: 0 = Sunday … 6 = Saturday. Defaults to the locale's, or Monday where the browser does not know it.

anatomy.name: Previous year
anatomy.description: A double chevron: twelve months back, or to the month of min. Disabled there.

anatomy.name: Previous month
anatomy.description: Disabled in the month of min. Mirrored right to left.

anatomy.name: Month
anatomy.description: The month and year in full, centred between the buttons. Announced as it changes.

anatomy.name: Next month
anatomy.description: Disabled in the month of max.

anatomy.name: Next year
anatomy.description: A double chevron: twelve months on, or to the month of max. Disabled there.

anatomy.name: Weekdays
anatomy.description: Two letters ("Mo"), or the narrow names ("T2") where the short ones are long; the locale's first day first.

anatomy.name: Day
anatomy.description: A button named by its full date.

anatomy.name: Outside day
anatomy.description: A day of the month either side, for shape: faded, hidden from assistive tech, never selected or banded.

anatomy.name: Selected day
anatomy.description: The value, or with range both ends.

anatomy.name: Unavailable day
anatomy.description: Before min, after max, or ruled out by isDateDisabled.

rows.property: Width and height on touch screens

whenToUse:
Use a Calendar where the day is picked by looking at the month: a booking
page, a delivery slot, a few weeks either side of today. Rule out the days
that cannot be picked with `min`, `max` and `isDateDisabled`, rather than
refusing the choice after it is made.

Month steps keep the day where they can: 31 January plus a month is 28
February, not 3 March.
whenNotToUse:
- **For a date far from today**, or one people know by heart, like a date
  of birth. Use a [Date Picker](?path=/docs/components-inputs-datepicker--docs):
  it takes the date typed, and opens this calendar when wanted.
- **For a span inside a form.** Use a
  [Date Range Picker](?path=/docs/components-inputs-daterangepicker--docs):
  it owns the two clicks that make a span and shows it here.
- **For a schedule of events.** A day here holds a number, not content.
  List the events in a [Table](?path=/docs/components-data-display-table--docs).

do.caption: A date close to now, where seeing the week matters: unavailable days are struck through before anyone picks them.

dont.caption: A date of birth is decades away: paging back a month, or even a year, at a time is slow. Type it in a Date Picker.

sections.title: Accessibility
blocks:
- A `role="grid"` named by the month and year ("September 2026"), with
  column headers that carry the full weekday name in `abbr`.
- Each day is a button named by its full date ("Friday 18 September
  2026"). The selected cell has `aria-selected`, and with `range` every
  cell from one end to the other does. Today has `aria-current="date"`.
- One tab stop: the selected day, or today when nothing is selected.
- Arrow keys move a day or a week, Home and End go to the week's ends,
  Page Up and Page Down move a month, and Shift+Page Up and Shift+Page
  Down a year. Enter or Space selects. Moving past the month shows the
  next one.
- Right to left, the arrows follow the screen (ArrowLeft is the next day)
  and the previous and next chevrons, single and double, are mirrored.

- The month and year are a polite live region, so paging is announced,
  by a month or by a year.
- The header's buttons are ordinary buttons in the tab order, before the
  grid: "Previous year", "Previous month", then after the month "Next
  month" and "Next year". The year buttons move the month shown by twelve
  months, or to the month of `min` or `max` when that is nearer.
- All four are disabled at the limits: the previous pair in the month of
  `min`, the next pair in the month of `max`.
- Unavailable days stay focusable with `aria-disabled`, so they are found
  and announced as unavailable rather than skipped. Enter on one does
  nothing.
- Days of the months either side are not buttons and are hidden from
  assistive tech.
- Today's figure measures at least 4.5:1 on its pill, in both modes, on
  its own and inside a range.

props.name: size
props.description: Padding 12, 16, 24 or 32px; the gap between children scales with it.

props.name: appearance
props.description: `elevated`: the card surface with a faint shadow. `outline`: the surface and its edge, no shadow. `unstyled`: keeps the padding and layout, drops every visual. `surface`: a block of a page on the Theme's canvas, elevated when the Theme's `contentStyle` is `card`, a section with a rule above when it is `flat`.

props.name: orientation
props.description: How children flow: `vertical` stacks them, `horizontal` sets them side by side (media and text).

props.name: isRounded
props.description: Rounds the corners with `--radius-lg`. Off: square corners.

props.name: hasBorder
props.description: The 1px `--color-border` edge. Off: no visible edge. `unstyled` never has one.

anatomy.name: Container
anatomy.description: The surface: --color-surface-raised, its --color-border edge and the padding from size. Content stacks or sits side by side, by orientation.

anatomy.name: Title
anatomy.description: Your content: a heading at the level the page needs. The card has none of its own.

anatomy.name: Body
anatomy.description: Your content: anything, here a line of muted text.

whenToUse:
Use a Card to group content about one thing, so it reads as a unit: a
person, a plan, a setting. Put headings inside at the level the page
needs; the card has none of its own.

A clickable card is one button, and a button may only hold phrasing
content: use spans for its title and text, not headings or paragraphs,
and put no links or buttons inside it. If a card needs its own actions,
leave it plain and put a button in it.

A card that navigates should be a link (`render={<a href />}`), not a
button with a click handler: a link opens in a new tab and shows its
address.
whenNotToUse:
- **For rows of data to compare.** Use a
  [Table](?path=/docs/components-data-display-table--docs): columns line
  values up, cards do not.
- **To show and hide content.** Use a
  [Collapse](?path=/docs/components-data-display-collapse--docs).
- **Just to add space or a background.** A plain `<div>` with padding
  does that without suggesting a unit.

do.caption: A plain card with its own Follow button: each control is reachable on its own.

dont.caption: A button inside a clickable card is invalid HTML, and neither control can be reached reliably.

sections.title: Accessibility
blocks:
- A plain card is a `<div>`: no role, no tab stop, nothing added to the
  accessibility tree.
- **A clickable card is one `<button type="button">`, so everything inside
  becomes its label.** Click, Enter and Space all call `onClick`.
- A link card is a real `<a href>`, in the tab order, with no `type`.
- The card has no heading of its own.
- Muted text clears 4.5:1 on every appearance, in both modes, at rest and
  on hover: hover changes the shadow or the edge, never the surface under
  the text. The `Contrast` story measures it.

props.name: label
props.description: The trigger's text, e.g. "Show details". Required.

props.name: openLabel
props.description: The trigger's text while open, e.g. "Hide details". Defaults to `label`. The button's name follows the state; `aria-expanded` says it either way.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Starting open state when uncontrolled.

props.name: size
props.description: The text size: `--text-body` (`md`) or `--text-body-sm` (`sm`). Match the text around it.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Dimmed, and clicking does nothing.

props.name: hiddenUntilFound
props.description: Keep the closed content in the page as `hidden="until-found"`, so the browser's find-in-page reaches it and opens it. Turn it off only for content that is expensive to render.

anatomy.name: Container
anatomy.description: Holds the trigger and the panel; sets the text size.

anatomy.name: Trigger
anatomy.description: A medium-weight text button, underlined on hover.

anatomy.name: Chevron
anatomy.description: Points right when closed and down when open. Decorative.

anatomy.name: Label
anatomy.description: The text. With openLabel, a second label replaces it while open.

anatomy.name: Panel
anatomy.description: The content, under the trigger. Its height animates open and shut.

whenToUse:
Use a Collapse for one aside in running content: billing details under a
plan, advanced settings under a form. It is a text button, not a bar,
because it belongs to the content around it, and its trigger reads like a
link in a sentence.
whenNotToUse:
- **As the structure of a page.** A list of sections needs real
  headings. Give each one a heading, in a
  [Card](?path=/docs/components-data-display-card--docs) section where it
  needs a frame, and put a Collapse under a heading only for the part
  that can wait.
- **For a short hint about a control.** Use a
  [Tooltip](?path=/docs/components-overlays-tooltip--docs) or a
  [Popover](?path=/docs/components-overlays-popover--docs), which do not
  push the page down.
- **For content most readers need.** Hiding it costs everyone a click.
  Show it.

do.caption: One aside, under the text it belongs to. The label says what opening it does.

dont.caption: Bare Collapses stacked with nothing around them read as a menu, not as asides. Give each section a heading, and a Collapse under it only for what can wait.

sections.title: Accessibility
blocks:
- The trigger is a `<button>` with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`
  pointing at the panel.
- Enter or Space toggles it. With `openLabel`, the button's name changes
  with its state ("Show details" / "Hide details"), and `aria-expanded`
  says it either way. Without it, the name stays the same.
- The chevron is decorative (`aria-hidden`), so it adds nothing to the
  name.
- Closed content is `hidden="until-found"` by default, so find-in-page
  reaches it.
- The trigger grows to a 44px target on coarse pointers.
- Under `prefers-reduced-motion` the panel and chevron change without
  animating.

props.name: label
props.description: The button's text and the popover's title.

props.name: resetLabel
props.description: The Reset button's text.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Open on first render, uncontrolled.

anatomy.name: Button
anatomy.description: An outlined secondary Button, "Columns", with a chevron. Opens the popover.

anatomy.name: Popover
anatomy.description: A Popover titled like the button, lined up with its end.

anatomy.name: Locked column
anatomy.description: The row header: always shown, so its box is ticked and disabled.

anatomy.name: Column checkbox
anatomy.description: One per column, named by its header, in table order. Ticked means shown.

anatomy.name: Reset
anatomy.description: A small ghost Button: brings back the default columns and calls onReset.

whenToUse:
Use a Column Chooser on a table with more columns than most people need at
once, typically six or more, where different people read different ones.
whenNotToUse:
- **To switch between whole layouts** (a summary and a detailed set): use
  saved views, so one choice changes several columns at once.
- **To filter rows.** Hiding a column does not hide rows; use filters in
  the table's toolbar.
- **For a table that fits.** If every column fits on the screens it is
  used on, leave them all shown.

do.caption: A few optional columns beside a locked name column.

dont.caption: A chooser for two columns: one is locked, so there is nothing to choose.

sections.title: Accessibility
blocks:
- The button reports `aria-haspopup="dialog"` and `aria-expanded`. The
  popup is a `role="dialog"` named by the label, "Columns".
- Opening moves focus into the dialog; Escape closes it and returns focus
  to the button.
- Each column is a checkbox named by its header, in table order; Space
  toggles it, and the shown keys are reported in column order, the row
  header always among them.
- The row header column's checkbox, and the last checked one, are
  `aria-disabled`: ticked and unchangeable.
- Reset is a button named "Reset" that brings back the default columns.

props.name: caption
props.description: Names the table for assistive tech. Visually hidden unless `showCaption`.

props.name: showCaption
props.description: Shows the caption above the table.

props.name: isSelectable
props.description: Adds a checkbox column, with a header checkbox that selects every row shown.

props.name: hasStickyHeader
props.description: Keeps the header row in view while the table scrolls inside its container, when something limits the container's height.

props.name: isResizable
props.description: A handle at the end of each column header that drags, or arrow-keys, the column wider or narrower (48 to 1200px). The table is then laid out by its header widths (`table-layout: fixed`): columns without a `width` share what is left, and what no longer fits is clipped.

anatomy.name: Caption
anatomy.description: Names the table. Visually hidden unless showCaption.

anatomy.name: Header row
anatomy.description: Small muted labels over a 2px rule, with no fill. Stays in view with hasStickyHeader.

anatomy.name: Sort button
anatomy.description: The whole header label, with an icon for the sort. Only on sortable columns.

anatomy.name: Select all
anatomy.description: With isSelectable. Selects or clears every row shown, and shows mixed when some are selected.

anatomy.name: Row
anatomy.description: As tall as what it holds: 28px for one line of text. No divider: tinted when hovered or selected.

anatomy.name: Row checkbox
anatomy.description: Named after the row header: "Select Atlas".

anatomy.name: Expand button
anatomy.description: With expandedContent: a ghost icon button. The chevron turns down when open.

anatomy.name: Row header
anatomy.description: The column marked isRowHeader, medium weight: the name a row is known by.

anatomy.name: Row actions
anatomy.description: With rowActions: a ghost "more" button at the end of the row that opens a Menu.

anatomy.name: Expanded row
anatomy.description: One cell spanning every column, under its row. Holds any layout.

anatomy.name: Total row
anatomy.description: With a footer on any column: a semibold row under a 2px rule, outside the sort.

whenToUse:
Use a Table for records that share their fields, when people compare them
or look one up: projects, invoices, members. Align numbers and dates to the
end, and mark the column a row is known by with `isRowHeader`.

**Sort cycles ascending, descending, off.** The third click returns to the
original order, which is often the one that meant something. Uncontrolled,
the table sorts a copy: dates as dates, numbers as numbers, text by locale
with "file 2" before "file 10". Empty values sort last both ways.

With server-side sorting, pass `sort` and `onSortChange` and hand back the
rows already sorted:

**Paging is not built in.** Put a
[Pagination](?path=/docs/components-navigation-pagination--docs) under the
table and pass it one page of `rows`. With `getRowId`, selection keeps
working across pages: "Select all" adds or removes this page's rows only.
Pass `expandedIds` to open rows from outside the table:

- **For records that do not share fields**, or that are read one at a
  time, like products in a shop. Use [Cards](?path=/docs/components-data-display-card--docs).
- **For layout.** A table announces rows and columns to a screen reader;
  use CSS grid to place things side by side.
- **For a spreadsheet**, where arrow keys move between cells and cells
  are edited in place. Table is a plain table, not an ARIA grid; the kit
  has no data grid yet.

dont.caption: Aligned to the start, 9 sits under the 1 of 1,203, and the column cannot be compared at a glance.

dont.caption: Without one, every checkbox is “Select row 1”, “Select row 2”: a screen reader user cannot tell what they select.

sections.title: Accessibility
blocks:
- A real `<table>` named by its `<caption>`, with `<th scope="col">`
  headers and a `<th scope="row">` for the row header column: screen
  readers announce the column and the row for every cell.
- Sortable headers carry `aria-sort` (`ascending`, `descending` or
  `none`); the sort control is a button inside the header.
- Row checkboxes are named after the row header ("Select Atlas"), or
  "Select row 1" without one, counted from `rows` so a sort does not
  rename them. The header checkbox is "Select all rows" and reports
  `mixed` when some are selected. A selected row has `aria-selected`.
- Each expand button is named after the row header ("Expand Atlas"),
  reports `aria-expanded`, and while open points at the content cell with
  `aria-controls`. Enter and Space toggle it. The name stays the same open
  or closed; `aria-expanded` carries the state.
- A row with nothing to expand has no button.
- The expand column's header is "Details", visually hidden, so the column
  is announced like the others.
- The content cell spans every column, so it is read as one cell under its
  row.
- Each row actions button is named after the row header ("Actions for
  Atlas") and reports `aria-haspopup="menu"`. Enter opens the menu,
  Escape closes it, and focus returns to the button. A row with no items
  has no button.
- The actions column's header is "Actions", visually hidden.
- When the table is wider than its box and nothing in it takes focus, the
  scroll box becomes a tab stop with a focus ring: `role="region"` named by
  the caption, which the browser scrolls with the arrow keys. A table that
  fits, or whose cells hold a control (a sort button, a checkbox), gets no
  extra tab stop.
- With `isResizable`, each column header holds a focusable
  `role="separator"` with `aria-orientation="vertical"`, named "Resize"
  and the header ("Resize Owner"), or the column's `key` when the header
  is not plain text. Its `aria-valuenow` is the column's
  width in px, between `aria-valuemin` 48 and `aria-valuemax` 1200.
- Arrow Right widens the column 16px and Arrow Left narrows it (mirrored
  in right-to-left); Home sets the narrowest width and End the widest.
  Dragging the handle does the same with a pointer.
- The total row is in a `<tfoot>` with one cell per column, so each total
  is announced under its column; the label column is its row header.

whenToUse:
Use a Field round a control that has no label of its own. Keep the helper
text to a line; put a longer rule behind `labelInfo`.
An **error** says what to change, not only that something is wrong.

A value people need to see but cannot change here (set by a rule,
another team or their role) stays a field: put `readOnly` on the control
and say in `helperText` why, and who can change it. Every Zweihänder
control takes `readOnly`. The boxed fields (Text Input, Textarea,
Search, Number Input, Select, Combobox, Date Picker, Date Range Picker)
all look the same: a filled box, still focusable, the value selectable
and submitted with the form. Checkbox, Radio, Switch and Rating keep
their look, since their mark is the value, and only stop changing.

- **Not disabled.** A locked value is still read and copied; a disabled
  one is not (Disabled, below, is for "not yet").
- **No lock icon by default.** The fill already marks the state, and an
  icon would need its own name for screen readers; the helper text says
  more than a lock.
- **A whole record that cannot be edited** is not a form of read-only
  fields: show it as a description list (`<dl>`), label and value with no
  box.

Disable a control only while it does not apply yet, and people can change
that on the same screen: a choice earlier in the form, a step not done.
Say what turns it on, in `helperText` or in the control that does it.

- **Disable for "not yet", hide for "not you", read-only for "not
  changeable here".** An action or a field people's role never lets them
  use, and that they do not need to read, is left out, not shown disabled:
  a control they can never turn on is noise and a support ticket. A value
  they need to see but may not change is read-only.
- **No tooltip for the reason.** A disabled control leaves the tab order,
  so a tooltip on it never opens by keyboard or on touch. Put the reason
  in text people can see; `labelInfo` stays active on a disabled Field.
- **Dimmed on purpose.** Disabled controls are exempt from contrast
  rules and drop below readable contrast, one more reason not to disable
  a value people need to read.
- **Fields that turn off together** each take `disabled`, and one line of
  text near them says what turns them on.
whenNotToUse:
- **Round a Zweihänder control.** Text Input, Textarea, Number Input,
  Select, Combobox, Date Picker, Checkbox, Switch and Radio have their own
  label, helper text and validation; a Field round one gives it two labels.
- **For a group of controls** under one name, use a `<fieldset>` and
  `<legend>`, or Radio's own group.

sections.title: Accessibility
blocks:
- The label is a real `<label>` for the control: it is the control's
  accessible name, and clicking it focuses the control.
- `helperText` is the control's description (`aria-describedby`), read
  after its name.
- A read-only control keeps its place in the tab order and has the
  `readonly` attribute, so screen readers announce it as read-only;
  typing does not change the value, and the reason in `helperText` is read
  as its description.
- A disabled control is left out of the tab order; its helper text is still its description, so a screen reader browsing to it
  hears why.
- `validationState="error"` sets `aria-invalid="true"` on the control.
  Colour is never the only signal: the helper text says what is wrong.
- The required asterisk is `aria-hidden`; put `required` on the control so
  screen readers announce it.
- The info button is named by `infoLabel` ("More information") and
  described by the label, so a list of buttons tells which field each is
  for. It sits outside the `<label>`: pressing it opens the note without
  focusing the control. Enter or a press opens the note, a dialog named by
  the label; Escape closes it and returns focus to the button.

sections.title: Accessibility
blocks:
- The input is a text field with `inputmode="numeric"` and the role
  description "Number field", named by the label.
- **Keyboard:** Up and Down step the value by `step` from the input; with
  Shift they step by 10, with Alt by 0.1. The steppers are out of the tab order
  (`tabindex="-1"`): the arrow keys do the same from the field.
- The steppers are named "Increase" and "Decrease" and are disabled at
  the limits, so a screen reader hears why nothing happened.
- The value is parsed and formatted in the user's locale; the form
  receives the plain number.

sections.title: Accessibility
blocks:
- The cells sit in a `group` named by the label; the label also names the
  first cell, and each later cell is named by `slotLabel`, "Character 2 of 6"
  by default.
- **Keyboard:** the group is one tab stop: only the cell to type into is in
  the tab order. Typing a character fills the cell and moves to the next;
  Backspace clears the cell before and moves back; Left and Right move
  between cells.
- Characters `validationType` does not allow are dropped, so letters cannot
  enter a numeric code.
- Pasting the whole code into any cell fills every cell; spaces are ignored.
- The first cell has `autocomplete="one-time-code"`, so phones offer the code
  from a text message.
- `helperText` is the group's description and `validationState="error"` sets
  `aria-invalid` on every cell.
- The resend button is disabled during the cooldown and its name carries the
  time left. After a send, focus moves to the first cell, so it is not lost
  with the disabled button; while a send is pending the button stays
  focusable and is marked `aria-busy`. The countdown is not a live region, so it does not interrupt
  every second.

- The field is named by its label. The Show / Hide button's name says
  what it does next and to which field ("Show password", "Hide new

- The rules are part of the field's description, each ending "(met)" or
  "(not met)", so they are read when the field gets focus; ticking one off
  is not announced on every keystroke.

  not keep the password as plain text in its form history.

  `new-password` where a password is chosen, so password managers fill or
  suggest the right one.

Use Search to find or filter: a list of components, a table, the whole
site. Say in the placeholder what is searched.

only the field: filtering a list in place does not need a landmark.
Give the page's main search `shortcut="/"`, and only that one.
whenNotToUse:
- **To find anything from anywhere in the app**, with recent items and
  results grouped by type. That is a command palette, opened with ⌘K, and
  the kit does not ship one. Do not bind ⌘K to a Search.
- **To choose one value from a list.** Use a
  [Combobox](?path=/docs/components-inputs-combobox--docs): it shows the
  matches and keeps the choice.

sections.title: Accessibility
blocks:
- `type="search"`, exposed as a `searchbox`, named by the visible label
  or "Search". A placeholder is not a name.
- **Clearing works the same everywhere:** the button, and Escape in the
  field (Chrome and Safari do this natively; Firefox did not). Either way
  `onChange` fires with a real event.
- The clear button is a real `<button>` named "Clear search", reached
  with Tab after the input. Pressed from the keyboard, it hands focus
  back to the field instead of losing it; a mouse press leaves focus
  where it was.
- The clear button's hit area grows to 44px on touch screens.
- The search icon is decorative and hidden from screen readers.
- **`shortcut`** focuses the field from anywhere on the page, without typing
  the key. It does nothing while focus is in a form field, or with ⌘,
  Ctrl or Alt held, or while the field is disabled or read-only. The input carries `aria-keyshortcuts`; the key cap is
  hidden from screen readers so the key is not read twice.
- The edge is the light `--color-border-input`, the approved exception to WCAG
  1.4.11 described on Text Input.

choices do not need to be compared side by side: a priority, a country
among a short list, a team member.

  them type to filter.

sections.title: Accessibility
blocks:
- The field is a `<button>` with `role="combobox"`,
  `aria-haspopup="listbox"` and `aria-expanded`; the list is a `listbox`
  of `option`s, with `aria-selected` on the chosen one.
- **Keyboard:** Space, Enter or Up/Down open it; the arrows move, typing
  jumps to a matching option, Enter selects, Escape closes, and focus
  returns to the field.
- The label is associated with the field (`aria-labelledby`). It is a
  `<div>`, because a `<label>` would also click the button and open the
  list.
- `helperText` is the field's description; `validationState="error"`
  sets `aria-invalid`, and `required` sets `aria-required`.
- **Read-only** locks the value, not the list: it still opens so the
  options can be read, but choosing one changes nothing. The field has
  `aria-readonly`. Use `disabled` when the list should not open at all.
- `isLoading` sets `aria-busy` on the field.
- The list renders in a portal at the end of `<body>`: it reads the
  root's tokens, so a `Theme` scope around the field does not restyle it.
- Options are 32px, 44px on touch screens.

whenToUse:
Use a Text Input for short free text on one line: a name, an email
address, a URL, a title. Give every field a visible label, and use the
placeholder only for a hint of the format.

**Errors** say what to change, in the helper text, next to the field. The
red edge only points at the message.

**Prefix or add-on.** A prefix is a hint inside the box, read past
without stopping: an icon, a currency sign. An add-on is a segment of its
own, for a fixed part long enough to label the value ("https://", ".com")
or for an action attached to it. Use one start and one end at most; a
field with an add-on and a prefix on the same side has two things before
the value to read.
whenNotToUse:
- **For several lines.** Use a
  [Textarea](?path=/docs/components-inputs-textarea--docs): Enter adds a
  line instead of submitting.
- **For a quantity.** Use a
  [Number Input](?path=/docs/components-inputs-numberinput--docs), which
  steps and parses. For numbers that are identifiers (postcodes, card
  numbers, phone numbers) keep the Text Input with `inputMode="numeric"`.
- **For a search query.** Use [Search](?path=/docs/components-inputs-search--docs),
  which clears and is exposed as a searchbox.
- **To pick from a known list.** Use a
  [Select](?path=/docs/components-inputs-select--docs) or a
  [Combobox](?path=/docs/components-inputs-combobox--docs).
- **For a unit people choose** (a currency, a country code). Add-ons take
  text or a `TextInputButton`, not a Select: put a
  [Select](?path=/docs/components-inputs-select--docs) beside the field.
- **For a date.** Use a [Date Picker](?path=/docs/components-inputs-datepicker--docs).

sections.title: Accessibility
blocks:
- The label is a real `<label>` for the input: clicking it focuses the
  input, and it is the input's accessible name.
- `helperText` is the input's description (`aria-describedby`), so a
  screen reader reads it after the name.
- `validationState="error"` sets `aria-invalid="true"` on the input.
  Colour is never the only signal: the helper text carries the message.
- `required` sets the native `required`; the asterisk is `aria-hidden`, so
  it is not read as "star".
- Do not rely on the placeholder as a label: it is not reliably announced
  and disappears as soon as anyone types. Without a visible label, pass
  `aria-label`.
- Pressing the field's padding, a prefix or a text add-on focuses the
  input, as a click anywhere on a native field does.
- A `TextInputButton` is a native `<button>` after the input in the tab
  order, pressed with Enter or Space. An icon-only one needs `aria-label`.
  Pressing it does not move focus to the input.
- `TextInputButton` is disabled with the field. In a read-only field it
  stays enabled, since opening or copying a fixed value is what it is for.
- **The edge is `--color-border-input`, about 1.5:1, a deliberate exception to
  WCAG 1.4.11** (approved 2026-10-08), for the light hairline of the
  Claude apps. The field is a white `--color-surface-raised` box on the off-white page, and the label, placeholder and focus ring mark it too.
  If your audience needs 3:1, set `--color-border-input: var(--color-border-bold)`.
- Focus ring: 2px, 2px offset, on click and keyboard alike.
- Heights are 32 and 40px, above WCAG 2.5.8's 24px minimum; a button in
  the field is a 24px target. The
  label is part of the target, since clicking it focuses the input.

`value` is out of `max`, and the value label shows the percentage:

Without a visible label, `aria-label` names the bar for screen readers.

blocks:
- `role="progressbar"` with `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin` and
  `aria-valuemax`, and `aria-valuetext` from Base UI. Indeterminate drops
  `aria-valuenow` rather than reporting 0.
- Every bar needs a name: a visible `label` (linked by Base UI) or
  `aria-label`.
- The fill clears 3:1 on the track for every variant and accent, in both
  modes. The value label is `--color-text-subtlest`.
- Under `prefers-reduced-motion` the fill stops easing between values and
  the indeterminate slide slows from 1.4s to 4s a pass.
- A progressbar is not a live region. If completion matters, announce it
  (a Toast, or a status message) when the task ends.
